items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: John Popkin didn‟t care as long the people came in and bought some drinks, he was cool.

ctx.x: and say give this guy a job for two weeks and then I will bring Louie Armstrong in for three days. He did that.

He was so funny though. The way I got him to book my trio was that I had been working at the Hickory House and I had gotten myself that job. But you know in those days I stayed on the job. I would go in for two weeks and stay for two years. So I was doing all right and John Popkin didn‟t care as long the people came in and bought some drinks, he was cool. So Joe Glazier sent a couple of his guys in to see me and say look we want to book you. So they got me a tour. So I am in Detroit and I am in Cleveland and in…
That was a great room there.
